title: Al-Mughni, the Enricher
tomorrow: rain cancels round two of the paint day. bad luck, or harm held back?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Ghaniyy, the Self-Sufficient, and Solomon's thank you that was for his own soul. The line: he needs nothing. Today's Name is the one who gives.
screen: `HE NEEDS NOTHING.` → `AND THE ONE WHO GIVES.`

segments.voice: A raise that's spent before it lands. A new phone, and then the next new phone. Enough has a way of moving, like the horizon when you walk toward it. Yesterday's question: why does one verse put rich and content side by side? It's in Surah an-Najm, in a list of things God does, and it's a strange little pair. Two verbs, one breath, as if getting more and having enough were two halves of the same gift.
screen: `ENOUGH KEEPS MOVING.` → `TWO VERBS, ONE BREATH.` → `MORE, AND ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: In Pickthall's words, it is He "Who enricheth and contenteth." Today's Name is Al-Mughni, the Enricher. So why pair the two? Here's the solution, from a hadith the Prophet, peace be upon him, gave in plain words: richness isn't having a lot of things; real richness is richness of the soul. The Arabic phrase is ghina an-nafs, the self that has enough. That's the piece to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, rich isn't a bank balance. It's a state of the soul. And it explains the verse. Riches without contentment never arrive; the horizon keeps moving. Contentment without anything at all is a different struggle. So Al-Mughni gives both: sometimes more, and sometimes the richer gift, the sense of enough. Notice this doesn't make asking wrong. The Prophet taught a prayer that asks for exactly this: suffice me with what is lawful instead of what is forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so that I need no one but You. Asking for more, and asking for enough, in the same sentence. Just like the verse.
screen: `WHO ENRICHETH AND CONTENTETH.` · `RICHNESS OF THE SOUL.` · `SOMETIMES MORE. SOMETIMES ENOUGH.` · `ENRICH ME BY YOUR BOUNTY.` · then, large: `HE ENRICHES.`

segments.voice: Rest both hands open on your knees, palms up, the posture of asking. If you pray, ask in your own heart for sufficiency, or use the Prophet's words: enrich me by Your bounty. Otherwise, name one thing that is already enough today, and let your open hands hold it until the bell.
screen: `PALMS UP.` · `ENRICH ME BY YOUR BOUNTY.` · `ONE THING THAT'S ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Al-Mughni. The Enricher, who gives riches, and gives the richer thing too: enough.
Hold this: he enriches, sometimes with more and sometimes with the feeling of enough. Fifteen sixty-three, done.

the Prophet said real richness is richness of the soul.

fork.setup: you finally buy the sneakers you saved for. two days later a friend shows up in the newer pair, and yours suddenly feel old. what does today's hadith point to?
options: save again; you'll feel rich once you own the newest pair.
richness is of the soul: your shoes didn't change, the comparison did.
get rid of them; owning nice things is the real problem here.
fork.reveal: the hadith puts richness in the soul, not the shoe rack. the verse asks for more and for enough; it doesn't make owning things wrong.

original.note: Arabic: the Enricher, from the traditional list of the Names; 53:48 says He enriches and contents.

trapdoor: what you thought: a God who makes people wealthy.
what it means: the Enricher, who gives riches and contentment, the richer gift.
what a scholar hears: 53:48 pairs aghna and aqna; Sahih al-Bukhari 6446 puts wealth in ghina an-nafs; the prayer for sufficiency is in Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3563.
guess: the Rewarder, who pays for good deeds
the Owner of the earth's treasures

chat.says: Eli left his sketchbook at the shop. it's GOOD. maybe better than mine. why does that bug me??
options: His gift doesn't shrink yours. Richness of the soul isn't a contest.
Because you need to practice more until you're better than him again.
Because he hasn't earned any praise yet, not after tagging the wall.
chat.meaning: The Prophet said richness is richness of the soul. Al-Mughni enriches and contents, and enough can be glad for someone else's gift.
